extracted.subtask_description: Practical craft and professional guidance for novelists — especially on producing long-form fiction through daily discipline, endurance, and cultivating an original voice. Emphasizes habits, reading, observation, and attitudes toward external validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality from Freedom
rubrics_metrics.description: Originality emerges not from technique but from refusing constraints — including the expectations of literary tradition, market, and ego.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is indeed something original about my novels, I think it springs from the principle of freedom. Resist imposed constraints and expectations; allow freedom to shape originality rather than relying solely on formal technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Reading Foundation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reading widely and constantly is non-negotiable for any aspiring writer; the novelist is first a reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The catalog of one's reading determines the range of one's writing. Prioritize broad, continual reading as foundational training rather than as optional background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observation Over Judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: "Be observant, but be slow to make judgments about those observations."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Take in detail and resist premature interpretation; premature judgment ossifies fiction. Honor observation and delay imposing meaning so material can reveal itself in the narrative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discipline of Daily Output
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent daily production is essential — Murakami's regimen: 1,600 words (10 Japanese manuscript pages) per day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work every day, stop when you could continue, and 'show up tomorrow.' The practical rule: set a concrete daily word/page goal, quit while still able to continue to preserve momentum for the next session.

rubrics_metrics.name: On Inspiration (Receptivity + Discipline)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be receptive to unbidden moments of inspiration, but recognize inspiration without discipline is nothing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the 'door open' every day so inspiration can be used; have routines and habits so that when inspiration appears you can act on it (anecdote: Murakami's inspiration was the crack of a baseball bat).

rubrics_metrics.name: Long-Form Endurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing the long novel is an athletic feat requiring physical and mental endurance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build endurance through routines (running, sleep, consistent schedule). Talent alone is insufficient for long-form work; cultivate bodily and psychological stamina to sustain long projects over years.

rubrics_metrics.name: On the Originality of the Self (Voice)
rubrics_metrics.description: A writer's voice cannot be borrowed or studied; it emerges only through patient excavation of one's own perceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid imitation: imitation yields competent prose, while surrendering to one's own oddity produces art. Develop voice by sustained self-exploration rather than trying to replicate others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attitude toward Awards and Reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Be indifferent to awards and contemporary reviews; the work judges itself over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat contemporary judgment as noise; focus on the work and its long-term reception rather than seeking immediate external validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing Schools and Technical Training
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing schools are useful for some and dispensable for others; no technique substitutes for the reader-writer dyad of self with chosen masters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use formal instruction selectively. Technical training cannot replace the personal process of engaging with chosen authors and developing one’s own relation to readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Three Faculties: Talent, Concentration, Endurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Three indispensable faculties for the novelist: (1) Talent (innate), (2) Concentration (cultivable), (3) Endurance (cultivable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize limits and possibilities: talent may be innate, but concentration (sitting at the desk for hours) and endurance (sustaining effort over years) can be trained and are crucial for success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluative Criterion — Unmistakable Voice
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel can be judged by whether it carries an unmistakable voice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess distinctiveness and authenticity of the narrator/authorial presence; a successful novel should present a voice that feels singular and persistent across the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluative Criterion — Sustained Internal Logic
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel should sustain its own internal logic over its full length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for consistency of rules, tone, world-building, and narrative logic from beginning to end; lapses in internal coherence weaken long-form fiction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluative Criterion — Honor Observation without Premature Judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: A novel should honor observation without imposing premature judgments on those observations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the text allows detail and experience to speak rather than forcing early interpretation; this pacing of judgment affects depth and ambiguity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluative Criterion — Open the World for the Reader
rubrics_metrics.description: A successful novel leaves the reader finishing feeling the world has been opened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure the novel by its capacity to expand the reader's sense of reality or perception; the ending should convey a lasting enlargement of experience or understanding.
